{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2024}}
'''Lomonosov's invariant subspace theorem''' is a mathematical theorem from [[functional analysis]] concerning the existence of [[invariant subspace]]s of a [[linear operator]] on some complex [[Banach space]]. The theorem was proved in 1973 by the Russian–American mathematician [[Victor Lomonosov]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Invariant subspaces for the family of operators which commute with a completely continuous operator|first1=Victor I.|last1=Lomonosov|journal=Functional Analysis and Its Applications|volume=7|pages=213–214|date=1973|issue=3 |doi=10.1007/BF01080698 }}</ref>

==Lomonosov's invariant subspace theorem ==

===Notation and terminology===

Let <math>\mathcal{B}(X):=\mathcal{B}(X,X)</math> be the space of bounded linear operators from some space <math>X</math> to itself. For an operator <math>T\in\mathcal{B}(X)</math> we call a closed subspace <math>M\subset X,\;M\neq \{0\}</math> an invariant subspace if <math>T(M)\subset M</math>, i.e. <math>Tx\in M</math> for every <math>x\in M</math>.

===Theorem===

Let <math>X</math> be an infinite dimensional complex Banach space, <math>T\in\mathcal{B}(X)</math> be [[compact operator|compact]] and such that <math>T\neq 0</math>. Further let <math>S\in\mathcal{B}(X)</math> be an operator that commutes with <math>T</math>. Then there exist an invariant subspace <math>M</math> of the operator <math>S</math>, i.e. <math>S(M)\subset M</math>.<ref>{{cite book|first1=Walter|last1=Rudin|title=Functional Analysis|date=1991 |publisher=McGraw-Hill Science/Engineering/Math|isbn=978-0070542365|page=269-270}}</ref>
